issue.title: Remove 32-bit architecture support
issue.body:
We have found few recent reports of 32-bit Bitcoin Core node use, yet we regularly run into problems with architecture-dependent types such as `size_t`.

- Reviewers must account for two integer widths even in ordinary size calculations.
  [Cache partitioning](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35616), [serialized-size validation](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2025/10/24/disclose-cve-2025-46597/), and [fee-estimator file checks](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34109) have all needed fixes for 32-bit overflow.
  Routine descriptor-parsing optimization also prompted [another review of Base58 arithmetic for 32-bit overflow](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35041#discussion_r4311175392).
- 64-bit sanitizer runs do not exercise 32-bit-only overflows, and [there is no supported way to run the integer sanitizer on ARM32](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32375#issuecomment-4825318068).
- 32-bit CI has needed [system-call workarounds](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35202) and [extra configuration and emulation work](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35230), and it [restricts the choice of CI providers](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35574#issuecomment-4989837570).
- Limited virtual address space requires separate [resource limits](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32530), [allocator workarounds](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/10120), and [database settings](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/12495).
  ARM32 alignment differences have also caused [an out-of-memory regression](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28913).
- Keeping 32-bit builds working has required [Qt compatibility patches](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29985) and [ARM32 reproducible-build workarounds](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/25643).

Previous discussions focused on shipping [32-bit x86 Linux binaries](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/17504) and [ARM32 release binaries](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/32375).
Keeping source support retains the [code and testing burden](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31425) even after binary distribution ends.

Given these recurring costs, I propose requiring a 64-bit target for Bitcoin Core node builds, including builds from source.
That would let us retire the 32-bit node CI and release configurations and simplify node code that exists only to accommodate 32-bit targets.

<details>
<summary>Further examples of the work created by 32-bit support</summary>

- [#33709](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/33709) and [#33724](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33724) replaced architecture-dependent serialized-size arithmetic after the published crash mitigation. The [review discussion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33724#discussion_r2476885390) explains the recurring need to reason about intermediate overflow and checked narrowing.
- [#35097](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35097) changed byte-unit literals because `size_t` prevented expressing larger storage sizes and limits on 32-bit targets.
- [#7848](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/7848) fixed UTXO hash results that differed between 32-bit and 64-bit builds because a `size_t` counter wrapped.
- [#24214](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/24214) made interpreter arithmetic independent of host width and reduced integer-sanitizer suppressions.
- [#34110](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/34110) exposed a 32-bit Base58 overflow during wallet fuzzing and documents the additional effort needed to reproduce it.
- [#30307](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/30307) needed different handling for file-position errors that occurred earlier on 32-bit systems.
- [#29415's review](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29415#discussion_r2556667714) revisited architecture-dependent counter types during private-broadcast work. [#32497's review](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32497#discussion_r2553107836) compared arithmetic across compilers and 32-bit/64-bit targets for a small allocation optimization.
- [#34108](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/34108) and [#34136](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34136) required changing a functional test whose memory-accounting assumptions failed on 32-bit builds. [#34132's review](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34132#discussion_r2679121949) needed different storage-corruption test setup because the 32-bit database path behaved differently.
- [#28531's test discussion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28531#issuecomment-2885251842) describes the difficulty of maintaining memory-usage expectations across both widths. [#35773](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35773) needed a sanitizer suppression for intentional hash truncation on 32-bit targets.
- [#16096](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/16096) raised declining developer testing and assumptions about `size_t`, `time_t`, and `long`. [#35466](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35466) later repaired ARM32 IPC test coverage that had been skipped because a dependency was missing.
- [#27879](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/27879#issuecomment-1591076522), [#31965](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31965#issuecomment-2708856306), and [the later hosting discussion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35574#issuecomment-4989837570) show ARM32 execution restricting CI hardware and provider choices. [#33302](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33302) needed an additional runner/cache exception.
- [#35546](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35546) revisited an i686 compiler choice originally made to avoid memory exhaustion. [#31772](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31772) records another 32-bit compiler/build-mode combination causing an IPC test failure.
- [#3324](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/3324) documents longstanding virtual-address-space exhaustion. [#28906](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28906) and [#28913](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28913) show ARM32 alignment assumptions causing a later memory regression.
- [#33333](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33333) needed arithmetic ordering chosen to avoid 32-bit overflow. [#34692](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34692) retained a separate 32-bit cache default. The unmerged [#35620](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35620) also illustrates separate database-cache behavior complicating proposed changes.
- [#2203](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/2203), [#2236](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/2236), [#438](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/438), and [#439](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/439) needed large-file accommodations for 32-bit builds.
- [#29980](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/29980) and [#29985](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29985) required dependency changes during the time64 transition. [#25573's ARM32 discussion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/25573#issuecomment-4509138869) describes extra toolchain and IPC work for static PIE.
- [#28096](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28096) found a nominally 32-bit build producing a 64-bit executable after losing target flags. [#22889](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/22889) and [#22923](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/22923) prompted additional 32-bit Clang coverage after compilation failures.
- [#18686](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/18686), [#19735](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/19735), and [#22464](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/22464) are smaller examples of warning and narrowing fixes needed specifically for 32-bit targets.
- [#15939](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/15939) and [#22908](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/22908) retired Win32 release and build configurations. [#18104](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/18104) stopped default i686 release builds while explicitly retaining source builds and CI, leaving later cleanup in [#19745](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/19745).
- [#23744](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/23744) removed an i686 Android target that had been broken unnoticed for months. [#24448](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/24448), [#24639](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/24639), and [#26075](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/26075) show the compatibility work and eventual cleanup around discontinued i686 release builds.
</details>

events.body:
Rough concept ACK.

I suppose this should happen eventually at some point. It's kind of a shame that we can't deprecate tier 1 support but leave this working in self-compilation, but if we did that we'd not get any of the cleanup benefits of dropping support...

What Pi devices do we think this would break support for? Seems like Pi 1 and 2 would be out of the mix, along with anybody running 32 bit Raspberry Pi OS on any device. Is that also your understanding?

Do we have any other major 32 bit users that we know about?
